subject: chemistry
pass: wave4 expert pass (Sonnet-equivalent CUET expert review, same procedure as waves 1 to 3)
scope: All 57 accepted chemistry questions of wave4-candidates-scored-2026-10-17.json (all engine-eligible per the acceptance engineer). Every question was solved independently first (numericals recomputed); then key, explanation, option length and grammar giveaways, wrong-direction traps, unit and chapter against data/nta_blueprints/chemistry.json (every pair verified by script), the 2026 CUET Chemistry syllabus PDF (data/CUET 2026/chemistry.pdf), ncert_ref, CUET level and time, and the content gates (hedge words, source-citing, missing figures, passage dependence) were checked. NCERT itself was not available (no network); the NCERT check is against the reviewer's knowledge of the current rationalised Class 12 Chemistry books (Part I Ch 1 to 5, Part II Ch 6 to 10). No model call, database or network was used.
notes: Verdict "drop" is not publishable; none of the 57 needed it. No syllabus drops: every topic maps to a line of the 2026 syllabus (Wurtz-Fittig and Fittig under chemical properties of haloalkanes and haloarenes, methanol poisoning under commercially important alcohols, azeotropes as an elementary idea, spin-only moments under CFT magnetic properties, hormones and vitamins under Biomolecules).

Systemic: 14 refs (all 8 Amines items and all 6 Biomolecules items) carry old-edition numbering ("Ch 13 Amines", "Ch 14 Biomolecules") beside rationalised Part II numbers for Ch 6 to 8; renumbered to Ch 9 and Ch 10. ncert_ref is in the content hash, so these need the same admit-on-expert-verdict treatment as the wave 3 text-only repairs. 13 of the 14 are text-only; the 14th (01d16929) is also the solver-visible repair below.

One repair changes solver-visible text (01d16929-b579-401b-9a88-81ff84f82232, statement C, one word: chiral). Under the wave-1 rule it needs a fresh blind re-solve; under the wave-2/3 rule for text-only repairs it does not. The reviewer re-solved it and the key (D, statements A, C, D) is unchanged.

Key position of the 57: A 15, B 14, C 14, D 14. The key is never the unique longest option by more than 14 percent (largest margin: item 45, 8 vs 7 characters, numeric options). No near-duplicate stems; the 4 questions of passage set w4-chem-02-set-1 (a fifth was rejected on solver agreement) are each self-contained given the passage and none refers to the dropped sibling.

Level: 12 are labelled hard; the heaviest are 5 (three named coupling reactions), 39 (Nernst with squared concentration), 49 and 57 (four-way comparisons). Each is a standard NCERT/board shape that fits about 90 seconds, so none is flagged above CBT level. The difficulty labels run a notch high for 35 and 49 (medium would be fairer); labels were left unchanged because they do not affect the solver text.

verdicts.why: Solved: SN2/hydrolysis rate follows leaving-group ability, I > Br > Cl > F, so B, D, A, C. Key C correct and unique; A and B are the polarity-order and F-first traps. C-X energies quoted (452, 234 kJ/mol) match the NCERT table.

Solved: (A) true, (B) true (chlorobenzene 1.69 D vs cyclohexyl chloride 2.04 D), (C) false (1-chlorobutane is lighter than water), (D) true (p-dichlorobenzene melts highest). Key A (A, B, D) correct and unique; all four statements are NCERT lines.

Solved: SOCl2 gives SO2 and HCl, both gases, so the product is pure; PCl5/PCl3 leave P compounds, HCl/ZnCl2 is the Lucas route. Key D correct and unique. The stem states the reason but the student must still know which reagent has gaseous by-products, so this is NCERT recall, not a leak.
Solved: covalent AgCN attacks through N, giving the isocyanide CH3CH2NC. Key B correct and unique (KCN would give the nitrile, AgNO2 the nitro compound). NCERT ambident-nucleophile line.

Solved: Wurtz-Fittig gives toluene, Fittig gives biphenyl, Wurtz gives ethane, so 3 hydrocarbons. Key B correct and unique. All three reactions are in NCERT Ch 6; top of the CUET range but a board staple, three short steps, within time.

Solved: Br2/CS2 cold gives o- and p-bromophenol (IV); chromic acid gives benzoquinone (I); conc. HNO3 gives picric acid (III); dilute HNO3 cold gives o- and p-nitrophenol (II). Key D (IV, I, III, II) correct and unique. Matches NCERT phenol reactions.
Solved: cumene process, air oxidation gives cumene hydroperoxide, then acid gives phenol and propanone. Key A correct and unique. Easy NCERT recall.

Solved: LiAlH4 reduces RCOOH to RCH2OH; NaBH4 does not reduce acids; Zn-Hg/HCl is Clemmensen; PCC oxidises. Key C correct and unique. Reduction of carboxylic acids is in the Ch 7 preparation of alcohols and the Ch 8 acid reactions (syllabus lists both).

Solved: methanol is oxidised to methanal then methanoic acid (NCERT methanol poisoning). Key D correct and unique; the other pairs mix ethanol's products in. Syllabus line: commercially important alcohols, methanol and ethanol.

Solved: PhONa + CH3Br gives anisole (Williamson); anisole brominates without FeBr3 in ethanoic acid, para major (NCERT). Key B correct and unique; tribromophenol is impossible because X is an ether. Two clear steps, within time.
Solved: the chain of four carbons with COOH at C-1 puts Cl on C-3, so 3-chlorobutanoic acid. Key A correct and unique; B is the wrong-end numbering, D the wrong chain.
Solved: HCN gives CH3CH(OH)CN; hydrolysis gives CH3CH(OH)COOH, 2-hydroxypropanoic (lactic) acid. Key A correct and unique.
Solved: RCOONa + soda lime gives R-H, so ethane from sodium propanoate. Key D correct and unique; butane is the Kolbe product, methane the ethanoate product.
Solved: acid supplies the acyl part, alcohol the alkyl part: CH3CH2COOCH3, methyl propanoate. Key C correct and unique.
Solved: formalin is 40 percent aqueous methanal (NCERT uses of aldehydes). Key B correct and unique. Easy NCERT recall.
Solved: (A) true, (B) true (NCERT: methanal, ethanal and propanone are miscible with water in all proportions), (C) true, (D) false (methanal is a gas, bp 252 K). Key C (A, B, C) correct and unique.

Solved: pKa 4-OCH3 4.47 > benzoic 4.20 > 4-Cl 3.98 > 4-NO2 3.44, so increasing acidity is C, A, D, B. Key A correct and unique. Substituent effect on acidity is an NCERT Ch 8 point; at the upper edge of CUET but fair and quick.
Solved: side-chain oxidation needs a benzylic H; n-, sec- and isobutyl have one, tert-butyl has none (NCERT: tertiary alkyl groups are not oxidised). Key D correct and unique.
Solved: dry HCl with excess CH3OH takes ethanal through the hemiacetal to the acetal CH3CH(OCH3)2, 1,1-dimethoxyethane. Key B correct and unique; the hemiacetal is only the intermediate.
Solved: LiAlH4 reduces C-N triple bond to CH2NH2, so CH3CH2NH2 (ethanamine). Key C correct and unique. Defect: ncert_ref uses the old edition number for Amines.
